what: Rules for filing two co-authored documents, 'Biological Load Accounting for Truck Drivers' and 'Decision-Exposure Coupling', as records with a checker. Committed before the documents, the records or the checker.
origin: two PDFs delivered by the owner in session, 2026-11-27, and the owner's 'Yes' to filing them here

rules.as_received: the two PDFs are kept byte for byte in as_received/, with the text pdftotext -layout gives beside each. Nothing in as_received/ is edited. The checker re-hashes all four files.
rules.records: records.json is built by build_records.py from the extracted text alone: each code block of a document is read as the Python literal it is written as. No value is typed by hand, corrected, completed or reworded. A block that cannot be read this way is listed as NOT_PARSED with the reason; it is not transcribed by hand to fill the gap.
rules.comments: a comment in a block (after #) is kept as text beside the block; it is not turned into a value.
rules.void: a None in a document is a void: it stays null. The checker lists every void with the comment the document puts on that line, or 'no reason given in the document'. A void is never read as False, zero or a default.
rules.need_states: the documents' core rule names four states for a need: PROVIDED, SELF_FUNDED, RESTRICTED, ABSENT. The checker reports every status value against them: one of the four; COMPOUND when the document joins two of them ('RESTRICTED or ABSENT', 'SELF_FUNDED / RESTRICTED'); OTHER_VOCABULARY for a value outside them (the ROLE block uses its own words). Nothing is mapped onto the four states by the checker; mapping is the authors' decision.
rules.status_tags: OBSERVED / DERIVED / PROPOSED tags are kept where the documents put them (section titles and comments). No tag is assigned here.
rules.arithmetic: the checker recomputes only figures the documents derive from their own numbers, with exact unit definitions (1 mile = 1609.344 m, 1 ft = 0.3048 m). A figure passes when it rounds to what the document states. Where a document does not give an input (the driving hours behind '300 a day is about 27 an hour'), the checker reports the value that statement implies and asserts nothing about it.
rules.external_figures: figures the documents attribute to outside studies or agencies are listed with source_state NOT OPENED. None was checked for this filing and none is restated from memory.
rules.true_cost: the core rule's true_cost adds self-funded costs, a value for restricted and absent needs, and responsibility hours. The per-need values are an open slot in the document and the terms have different units, so the checker reports true_cost as NOT_COMPUTABLE and never as a number.
rules.two_documents: both documents carry a PROVENANCE block and a false-denominator definition, and they differ. Both are kept as written. The checker reports the differences; which document owns the shared blocks is an open item for the authors.
rules.no_person: no person, carrier, shipper or site is named in the records beyond what the documents name.

amendments.name: second delivery of both documents (v2)
amendments.after: branch biological-load-accounting at 2167927. The owner delivered a revised PDF of each document. Declared before the v2 files, records or checker changes are committed.

rules.versions: the first delivery stays where it is, unedited: as_received/ and its records, now named records_v1.json (same bytes). The second delivery goes in as_received_v2/. records.json is built from the current delivery (v2) and names what it supersedes. The checker re-hashes both deliveries and rebuilds both record files.
rules.what_changed: reported by the checker from the two extracted texts, block by block; nothing is carried from v1 into v2 by hand.
rules.pointers: in v2 the truck-driver document no longer carries its own PROVENANCE block and gives its false-denominator definition and status as 'canonical in Decision-Exposure Coupling'. The checker treats such a value as a pointer and checks that it resolves: the coupling document must carry a PROVENANCE block and a FALSE_DENOMINATOR block with that field. A pointer that does not resolve is a FAIL. This replaces the open item 'which document owns the shared blocks'; the authors have answered it.
rules.void: v2 states the rule itself ('None = unassessed (void): neither pass nor fail'). The earlier rule here says the same and stays.
